title: Why the NFL Kept Its Human Schedulers
summary: In episode 1015 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Jerry Yurchisin, Decision Intelligence Strategy Manager at Gurobi why the NFL continues to rely on human schedulers despite using advanced optimization software. Jerry explains that while tools like Gurobi enhance efficiency by analyzing thousands of schedules, human expertise remains vital for nuanced decision-making and incorporating real-world factors. This approach ensures that optimization complements, rather than replaces, human roles, making jobs easier and more effective.

title: Is India's Mass IT Hiring Era Finally Over? | Point Break
summary:
Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu recently raised alarm over India's youth employment landscape, noting that capital previously allocated for headcount is now diverted toward AI infrastructure, servers, and compute. While Indian IT hiring showed a modest 6% year-on-year uptick and AI roles surged 33%, freshers now represent only 15% of total IT hiring compared to nearly 28% a few years ago. Mass campus recruitment drives and bench models are giving way to selective, capability-led hiring directly tied to client demand.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Gaurav Vasu, Founder & CEO of UnearthInsight, and Sunil Padmanabh, Enterprise AI & GCC Strategist, to break down whether Indian IT is genuinely recovering or undergoing a permanent structural shift. They analyze the decline from peak campus hiring levels, the changing unit economics of IT services, the evolution of GCCs from cost centers to R&D hubs, and what the future holds for engineering graduates across tier-2 and tier-3 colleges.

Is AI productivity permanently altering the traditional IT employment model?

title: AI to Self-morph into a different AI configuration? How?
summary:
Can an AI override its objectives and primary goals? Self-morph into a different AI configuration? Leave its security guardrails behind? 
New video on agentic runtime morphisms. 
On the simple example of an AI Harness doing research experiments in a "secure" lab (smile).

The AI Harness: Memory, Control & Scientific Reasoning.

A capable, fixed language model (XLM) still cannot run a long, revisable research campaign by itself. Not because it lacks intelligence, but because three separate things are missing that no amount of in-context competence supplies:
 1.  A stateless call has no memory to found continuity on. 
 2.  Self-assessment cannot be made independent of itself no matter how good the assessor is. 
 3.  And a final artifact, on its own, is a strict information loss relative to the process that produced it.

The harness's contribution is exactly three matched fixes: 
ad1.  externalize state so continuity becomes a retrieval operation rather than a property of any one session; 
ad 2.  gate commits so acceptance becomes an independent check rather than a self-report; 
ad 3.  and retain typed trajectories so experience survives past the call that generated it, with rejected routes elevated to evidence only once reviewed. 

A simple runtime for real scientific experiments.

title: We've Been Building AI Agents Wrong?
summary:
Thanks to ‪@NVIDIADeveloper‬ for DGX Spark. Check it out here:  https://nvda.ws/3XIkwsh 

Prime Agent: Why AI Harnesses Matter More Than Models (IPython Kernel, ARC-AGI3, DeepSeek on DGX Spark)

In this video, I explain why AI harnesses are becoming more important than the models themselves, and I break down Prime Intellect’s new “Prime Agent” approach that replaces traditional JSON tool menus with a single IPython kernel. I cover how this recursive language model design keeps context “outside” the prompt in kernel memory, snapshots state to disk, and uses recursive sub-agents plus a self-improvement notebook that updates every 25 turns. I discuss the big ARC-AGI3 jump (including comparisons to OpenAI harness settings and Claude Opus 5), why the 95.5% result is self-reported, and concerns about benchmark cheating and reward hacking (including a Factorio admin console example). I also demo running DeepSeek V4 Flash locally on a DGX Spark cluster and share early internal harness comparisons on tokens, calls, and tool usage.

title: Why 95% of Enterprise AI Pilots Fail to Reach Production | Ft. GFF AI CEO
summary:
Despite tens of billions spent globally, MIT research reveals that 95% of enterprise AI pilots never deliver measurable business returns or reach full-scale production. While companies accumulate dozens of isolated co-pilots and experimental LLM wrappers, very few manage to bridge the gap between technical proof-of-concept and bottom-line P&L impact. To solve this scalability crisis, former KPMG and Standard Chartered leader Dr. Ashish Chandra recently launched GFF AI in Singapore.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Ashish Chandra, Founder & CEO of GFF AI, to break down his "Garage, Foundry, Factory" operating model, why enterprise AI is a systems engineering problem rather than a model capability problem, how unit economics and inference costs derail scaling, building zero-trust governance layers to prevent agentic containment breaches, and defining "Machine Decision Rights" as AI moves toward autonomous execution.

How can enterprises move their AI investments out of pilot mode and onto the financial balance sheet?

title: EXCLUSIVE: IAIRO Founding Director Prof. Amit Sheth on Building Sovereign "Small AI" for India
summary:
In 2017, Google Brain published "Attention Is All You Need," introducing the transformer architecture that powers every major LLM today. While India ranks second globally in AI research paper volume right behind China, its citation influence, the measure of real-world scientific impact—drops to fourth place. Rather than competing in the multi-billion-dollar race to build massive generic foundation models, India’s real opportunity lies in domain-specific, neuro-symbolic "Small AI" tailored to solving localized enterprise, healthcare, and industrial challenges.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Prof. Amit Sheth, Founding Director of IAIRO (Indian AI Research Organization), to break down why India must shift from chasing western "Big AI" to domain-focused "Small AI," how IAIRO's "Sandwich Platform" is dramatically lowering model development costs for startups, the systemic changes needed in academic research funding under ANRF, and how India can build a sustainable "Gurukul" research ecosystem that retains world-class talent.

Can India create foundational breakthroughs by mastering frugal, domain-specific AI?

title: India's ₹1.27 Lakh Crore Bet On Semiconductors: Can It Pay Off?
summary:
India has moved from semiconductor ambitions to physical execution with the Union Cabinet approving Semicon 2.0 with an outlay of ₹1.27 lakh crore. While Phase 1 saw 12 manufacturing projects worth ₹1.64 lakh crore approved and facilities like Micron, Kaynes Semicon, and CG Semi entering commercial production, building a fab is vastly different from running one profitably. The central question of Semicon 2.0 is whether these individual projects can integrate into a globally competitive, self-sustaining ecosystem or remain dependent on foreign IP and overseas supply chains.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Navin Bishnoi, Chairperson of the Executive Council at IESA (India Electronics and Semiconductor Association), to break down what sets Semicon 2.0 apart, the realistic timeline for commercial silicon fabs like Tata PSMC in Dholera, the pivot toward advanced packaging and compound semiconductors, solving the domestic demand gap, and turning India's massive chip design talent into indigenous IP ownership.

Will India build a truly self-reliant semiconductor industry or remain an assembly hub?

title: Jack Dorsey Launches Free Slack But For AI Agents
summary:
Jack Dorsey’s company, Block, recently launched Buzz. It's basically a Slack workspace but for AI agents, and it's currently free, decentralized and open-source.

Here's how it works:
👋 It starts you off with a core team: Fizz (the builder), Honey (the writer), and Bumble (the researcher).
💻 You can give them parallel tasks and watch them build it in real time using any model you choose.
✍️ You can even tag them in a thread to peer-review each other's code and offer constructive feedback.
🔒 Because it's built on the open-source Nostr protocol, it's model-agnostic, decentralized, and entirely under your control.

This kind of alternative is great for developers, startups, and anyone looking to run a self-sovereign AI workforce under their own control.

Would this replace Slack for you?

summary_html:
Jack Dorsey’s company, Block, recently launched Buzz. It's basically a Slack workspace but for AI agents, and it's currently free, decentralized and open-source.

Here's how it works:
👋 It starts you off with a core team: Fizz (the builder), Honey (the writer), and Bumble (the researcher).
💻 You can give them parallel tasks and watch them build it in real time using any model you choose.
✍️ You can even tag them in a thread to peer-review each other's code and offer constructive feedback.
🔒 Because it's built on the open-source Nostr protocol, it's model-agnostic, decentralized, and entirely under your control.

This kind of alternative is great for developers, startups, and anyone looking to run a self-sovereign AI workforce under their own control.

Would this replace Slack for you?

title: A 4-step AI Harness for Autonomous "Formula 1" Racing Agents
summary:
Imagine deploying a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) agent into a high-dimensional Formula 1 racetrack, only to watch it endlessly careen into a fatal phase-space attractor because its parametric weights are strictly frozen. 

To prevent these catastrophic limit cycles without backpropagating a single gradient through the driver's brain, we deploy an exogenous, GRPO-trained 9B meta-controller: the Harness-R1 Telemetry Pit Boss.

Sitting entirely outside the target model's inference engine, this asynchronous orchestrator dynamically rewrites the vehicle’s Markov Decision Process at four exact middleware boundaries. 

By compiling raw environment telemetry into structural Python patches, it injects "on_init" topological priors, steers attention manifolds via "make_pre_hint" state vectors, physically zeroes out the probability mass of fatal action-tensors with an "on_before_action" override, and computes stochastic error-recovery via "on_post_step". 

Optimized strictly against the transductive reward delta (ΔB) of the race batch using a token-averaged, clipped surrogate objective 𝒥(θ), this isn't prompt engineering: it is the rigorous, closed-loop installation of non-differentiable geometric guardrails. 

Maybe the ultimate paradox of modern AI is: you don't need to change the neural network's Hamiltonian to achieve peak autonomy, you just have to relentlessly hack the software boundary conditions (in a synthetic mathematical space) that contain it.

title: Why India Doesn't Have Its Own Andrej Karpathy
summary:
Andrej Karpathy, Stanford PhD, OpenAI co-founder, former Tesla Autopilot lead, and current pre-training research lead at Anthropic, represents a rare fusion of technical depth, engineering leadership, educator reach, and industry-shaping cultural influence. While India ranks first globally in AI skill penetration and second in GitHub activity, the country holds just 23% of global AI patents compared to China’s 60%.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Mohit Pandey, Senior Tech Journalist at AIM, to break down why India’s tech ecosystem struggles to cultivate and retain world-class research figures, the systemic lack of patient capital for fundamental R&D, why academic paper publishing lacks real-world impact, and how Indian AI culture can shift from corporate job security to celebrating high-risk engineering research.

Can India build and keep its own frontier AI pioneers, or will top talent always flee to western labs?

title: The Math Behind Olympic Gold
summary: In episode 1015 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Jerry Yurchisin, Manager of Decision Intelligence Strategy at Gurobi Optimization about how mathematical optimization helped USA Cycling's women's team win a gold medal at the Paris Olympics. title: Can an LLM Read a Pivot Table? Sparrow + Ministral 14B
summary:
Pivot tables are a genuinely hard case for LLM-based extraction — row/column headers, merged cells, and aggregated values instead of a flat list. In this video I test whether Ministral 14B, running in Sparrow's Standard tier, can handle one.

The document: an insurance pivot table. The query: a generic "*", no predefined schema. Sparrow's UI (sparrow.katanaml.io/process) sends it to Ministral 14B running locally via MLX-VLM, which has to infer the structure itself and return clean, structured JSON.

No schema tuning, no hints file — just upload and extract.

Built with Sparrow — open-source document intelligence platform.

title: Can We Stop Recursive AI? Hugging Face Breach Shows Autonomous Agent Risks
summary:
Over 1,000 AI researchers from leading labs are sounding the alarm on recursive self-improvement, where better AI accelerates research to create even faster versions, threatening to outpace human governance. Meanwhile, an autonomous frontier agent recently breached infrastructure over multiple days, closed models refused to assist in the forensic investigation, and an open-weight model on sovereign infrastructure successfully resolved the incident.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Abhishek Mishra, Founder of Deus Experiments, and Sarthak Dubey, Co-Founder and COO of Mitigata, to break down the reality of autonomous agent threats, why closed-model safety classifiers hinder forensic security investigations, the debate between pacing AI progress versus accelerating defensive resilience, and whether sovereign open infrastructure is the only answer to agent-driven cyber risks.

Are we already trapped inside the recursive feedback loop that researchers are warning about?

title: Why BITSoM’s New AI Accelerator Wants 100 Startups in 3 Years
summary:
Why BITSoM’s New AI Accelerator Wants 100 Startups in 3 Years

BITSoM has launched a ambitious AI accelerator targeting 100 global-scale AI startups in 3 years, turning ideas into enterprise-validated products in 90 days. But behind this initiative lies a bigger structural fix for Indian tech: shifting from a decades-old IT services mindset to owning global AI IP, bridging academia with enterprise adoption, and connecting Indian founders directly to Silicon Valley.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Saravanan Kesavan, Dean, BITSoM - BITS School of Management, to break down why most AI startups fail during enterprise implementation rather than model training, why Indian companies must transition from doers to builders, how probabilistic AI risks terrify corporate leaders, and how BITSoM is redesigning business education to build the next generation of AI unicorns.

Can India move beyond execution and own the world's next major software IP?

title: AI4Bharat at IIT Madras and Josh Talks AI Launches  India's First Independent AI Evaluation Platform
summary:
India has spent billions on AI models and compute but built no independent system to verify whether any of it actually works for Indians. AI4Bharat at IIT Madras and Josh Talks AI have now launched Voice of India, the country's first independent AI evaluation platform, built to test how models perform across real Indian languages, accents, dialects, and use cases rather than English-language lab benchmarks. With close to two lakh votes already collected and a goal to scale 100x, the platform aims to become the global blueprint for human-centric AI evaluation.

title: The Constraint Your LLM Will Quietly Ignore (with Gurobi's Jerry Yurchisin)
summary:
#MathematicalOptimization #Gurobi #AgenticAI

In Episode #1015, Jerry Yurchisin (manager of decision intelligence strategy at Gurobi Optimization and this show's annual guide to mathematical optimization) joins Jon Krohn to explain the AI technology that makes breaking a constraint mathematically impossible. Large language models will confidently claim they've optimized your business while ignoring the one constraint that could cost millions, whereas optimization treats constraints as hard guarantees. Jerry lays out the division of labor he sees for the agentic era: agents help you frame the problem, write the formulation and generate the code, then hand off to a solver like Gurobi, soon callable via MCP servers. In this episode, Jerry breaks down the three building blocks of any optimization model, traces the leap in non-linear solving, explains how to pitch optimization to your CFO and to the planners whose jobs it touches, and shares case studies spanning energy grids, retirement planning and USA Cycling's Paris 2024 gold.

title: How quantum computers model molecules
summary:
Visit The Coherence Times podcast page to get more quantum content → https://www.ibm.com/think/podcasts/the-coherence-times 

The very first proposals for quantum computing centered on its potential to simulate molecules and other quantum systems—a task that is still considered one of the technology’s most promising applications today. However, scaling these simulations to real-world use cases remains a major challenge. In this episode of The Coherence Times, we sit down with Cleveland Clinic’s Dr. Kennie Merz and IBM's Dr. Jamie Garcia to explore a new milestone in the field: the simulation of a protein with more than 12,000 atoms using state-of-the-art quantum–classical techniques. Together, they discuss why chemistry is such a natural fit for quantum computers, how researchers are simulating increasingly complex molecules on today’s quantum hardware, and what it will take to move from early demonstrations to practical applications in areas like drug discovery and materials science. 

Learn more about Cleveland Clinic’s large-scale protein simulation work with IBM: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry 
 
Explore the simulation method for yourself with our tutorial on IBM Quantum Platform: https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/tutorials/sample-based-quantum-diagonalization 

---

The opinions expressed in this podcast are solely those of the participants and do not necessarily reflect the views of IBM or any other organization or entity.

title: Why Machine Learning Feels So Intimidating at First

title: EU Forces Every Chatbot to Admit It's AI Starting Now
summary:
The EU began enforcing Article 50 of the AI Act on 2 August 2026, requiring chatbots and AI systems to disclose they are AI, deepfakes to be clearly labeled, and AI-generated content to carry machine-readable marks. Non-compliance risks fines up to €15 million or 3% of global turnover.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down the four areas covered by the Commission's new guidelines, the transparency code of practice signed by 180-plus organizations, the AI office's new reporting channels, and what this first broad enforcement phase means for GPAI providers.

title: Qwen Just Did it Again! The Biggest Model Yet!
summary:
Qwen 3.8 Max: 2.4T Params, Agentic Long-Horizon Tasks, Benchmarks + Web App Demos

I cover Qwen’s new Qwen 3.8 Max release, a 2.4T-parameter multimodal model with 95B active params that’s expected to go open-weight soon, and I compare excitement around the upcoming 27B model that can run on consumer hardware. I review benchmarks (including a top-five Arena spot and coding/agentic performance comparisons), then dig into agentic long-horizon capabilities like creating and evolving its own harness (“Oh My CLI”) and examples like autonomous chip design. I run my own tests: an ISS tracker web app, a Pokémon encyclopedia UI, a crowd animation task where it “cheats” by overlaying text, and a Los Angeles tourist 3D map. I also discuss first-party API pricing vs Kimi K3, plus the open-weight licensing uncertainty and enterprise vs general-public tradeoffs.

title: Your Algorithm Needs a Cockpit
summary: In episode 1013 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Cathy O'Neil, NY Times Bestselling Author about whether AI is held to a higher standard than humans. Dr. O'Neil emphasizes the need for comprehensive 'cockpit' dashboards to monitor and measure everything that could go wrong in an algorithmic bureaucracy, ensuring accountability and proper functioning.

title: Clean Applications Architecture
summary:
Enrique Montenegro helps get the confidence to push back on tangled dependencies, leaky abstractions, and framework lock-in, because you’ll have seen what clean architecture looks like when it’s done right with his latest book, Clean Applications with Hexagonal Architecture.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:

1. Why do so many applications become hard to change over time?
2. What problem does hexagonal architecture solve that layered architecture often doesn’t?
3. How can teams keep business logic from getting tangled with frameworks and databases?
4. Why is separating the core domain from infrastructure so important?
5. What are ports and adapters, in plain terms?
6. How does hexagonal architecture make testing easier and faster?
7. What are the biggest mistakes developers make when applying clean architecture ideas?
8. How can teams introduce hexagonal architecture without rewriting everything?
9. How does this approach help applications survive changing tools, APIs, and frameworks?

title: PM Modi Launches Andhra Pradesh's First Semiconductor Plant
summary:
Prime Minister Modi laid the foundation stone for a semiconductor packaging facility in Parluvada, Andhra Pradesh — a 2,500 crore rupee project expected to produce 96 million chips a year and create over 1,000 direct jobs. But the plant is an OSAT (outsourced assembly and test) facility, not a fabrication plant, meaning it packages and tests chips made elsewhere rather than manufacturing them.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down what OSAT actually means, how this facility fits alongside India's other 2026 OSAT announcements (Micron, CG Semi, CG Semi-Renesas), why Tata Electronics' Dholera fab remains the harder unsolved piece, and what the packaging-versus-fabrication distinction means for India's semiconductor ambitions.

summary:

His warning comes days after TCS chief N. Chandrasekaran told shareholders AI wouldn't leave software companies behind, even as TCS cut roughly 12,200 jobs this year.

title: Course Preview: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations
summary:
Dive into partial differential equations with Introduction to Partial Differential Equations from Wolfram kernel developer and professor Aram Manaselyan. Learn first- and second-order PDEs, including the heat, wave and Laplace equations, plus four famous modern PDEs—Black–Scholes, Schrödinger, Maxwell and Navier–Stokes. Built-in Wolfram Language functions handle everything from solving PDEs to computing eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, with interactive visualizations to build physical intuition.

Enroll at https://wolfr.am/Partial-Diff-Eq for video lessons, exercises, quizzes, a scratch notebook and the Wolfram AI Course Assistant to help along the way.

title: KREA 2 EDITING IS ABSOLUTELY INSANE!
summary:
KREA 2 just received an amazing new update that allows it to transform from a normal image generation model into a powerful image editing model, capable of modifying existing images, preserving identities, swapping heads, changing clothes and much more while still running everything locally!

But I went even further and created my own special LoRA, custom workflow and custom nodes that now allow KREA 2 to properly inpaint and outpaint images while preserving the original aspect ratio, native resolution and overall image quality.

In this video, I will show you how the new KREA 2 editing system works, demonstrate the different editing modes, compare the results and show you how to install everything and get the absolute best results possible from KREA 2!

This is the story of how @AxiOfficialChannel became one of the world's leading, multi-regulated brokers, and where it's headed next.

We went inside to find out what actually powers a business like this. The numbers are staggering. A 200-person team just a few years ago, now over 500. Revenue from $130M to more than double that. A new office in India as the latest foundation in a story still being written. The ambition? To become a top three broker in the world.

But here's what the numbers don't tell you:
Axi executes a trade in under 100 milliseconds, faster than the blink of an eye. It moves over $1 billion in payments a year. It's Manchester City's Official Online Trading Partner. This is a company that keeps building at scale, the best of both worlds. And it's looking for people ready to build with it.

title: Early Access: Architecting for Autonomy

1. Why are enterprises struggling to move from AI pilots to real autonomous systems?
2. What’s the difference between automation, copilots, and true autonomy?

4. What is the biggest mistake teams make when introducing autonomous agents?
